This solicitation is being issued under Emergency Acquisition Flexibilities (EAF), formerly known as SEPA. Drawings and technical data are not available for this solicitation/requirement. This requirement requires Government source approval. Quotes/proposals received from sources which are not Government-approved sources of supply will be deemed technically unacceptable, and therefore ineligible for award. Quotes/proposals from dealers/distributors for government approved source(s) MUST submit a copy of their authorized distributor letter (on the actual manufacturer?s letterhead) to the buyer/point of contact indicated on the solicitation via email, at time of quote/proposal submittal. NAVSUP WSS Code N2 has determined that the requirements at DFARS 211.274 whichmandates the use of DFARS clause 252.211-7003 "Item Unique Identification and Valuation" in all solicitations and contracts, be deleted from all non-CLSSAFMS spares requirements processed by NAVSUP WSS and DLA-Aviation. The affected parts are wholly owned by FMS customer countries, arenot covered by a Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangement (CLSSA), thesesame assets will be delivered to the customer country for their sole use. The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. The FMS customer countries retain ownership of their parts throughout the asset's lifecycle. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. Based on this, there is no needfor these non-CLSSA FMS country assets to be specially marked for tracking by DoD. All potential offers shall provide newly manufactured spares only. Refurbished, remanufactured, or repaired material will not be acceptable;Offers for such are ineligible for award. Offerors are advised that offers received from sources which are not government-approved sources of supply will be deemed technically unacceptable, and therefore ineligible for award. Any distributors of approved source(s) MUST submit a copy of their authorized distributor letter, on the source?s letterhead, to the buyer point of contact indicated on the solicitation via email, at time of proposal submittal.

title: Portrait Photography Concessionaire Services � Defense Depot Richmond, VA
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Family & Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (FMWR), a Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI), is soliciting quotes for Portrait Photography Services for children enrolled at the DLA Child Development Center (CDC) located at Defense Supply Center Richmond (DSCR), VA. IMPORTANT NOTICE TO OFFERORS: This is a non-appropriated fund (NAF) concessionaire (revenue-generating) procurement. The Government will NOT pay for these services. The successful contractor will be compensated solely through their awarded share of gross revenue collected from portrait package sales to CDC patrons. All customer payments will be processed exclusively through the official DLA FMWR Point of Sale (POS) system. The Contractor must propose a single, uniform DLA FMWR Commission Percentage of Gross Revenue (remitted to the NAFI), which will remain firm-fixed for the duration of the contract (including all option periods). Scope of Services The Contractor shall conduct a minimum of three on-site portrait photography events per contract year: One (1) Fall CDC Portrait Event (Estimated volume: 90�110 children) One (1) Spring CDC Portrait Event (Estimated volume: 90�110 children) One (1) CDC Graduation Portrait Event (Estimated volume: 20�25 children) Note: Stated participation volumes are non-binding estimates and do not guarantee sales. Contract Type and Period of Performance This solicitation is expected to result in a single-award, commercial concessionaire contract with: Base Period: January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2027 Option Periods: Four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods (extending through December 31, 2031), exercised at the sole discretion of the Government. Vetting and Security Requirements Because this contract involves direct interaction with minor children within a military Child Development Center, strict vetting and child protection mandates are enforced. Every contractor employee entering the CDC must successfully pass background investigations (NACI/T1C, FBI fingerprinting, and 5-year state criminal history checks per DoDI 1402.05) at the Contractor's expense. Additionally, all on-site personnel must possess REAL ID-compliant identification. Critical Deadlines Written Questions Deadline: Questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing via email to the Contracting Officer at Elizabeth.Kostos@DLA.mil no later than November 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) to allow sufficient response time. Quote Submission Deadline: Quotes must be received in full no later than December 18, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST).

title: Market Intelligence Notice � Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB)
description: Market Intelligence Notice � Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.0 Objective The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District (SAS) is seeking market intelligence to identify and assess industry capabilities relevant to the construction of various facilities on military installations utilizing the Pre-Engineered Metal Building construction methodology. The Government is pursuing modern industrialized construction approaches intended to improve schedule, cost, and lifecycle outcomes for this facility type. For purposes of this RFI, respondents should clearly identify whether they view these features as: Fully compatible with their standard commercial or industrialized building system; Achievable with modifications; or Better addressed through an alternative technical solution that provides equal or better performance. Where respondents recommend alternatives, the response should explain how the proposed approach would satisfy or improve upon the Government's desired performance outcomes for schedule; cost; capacity/readiness; quality and durability; energy consumption; repeatability/scalability; site and installation impact; and compliance/turnover. Information provided by respondents will be used to help the Government understand available market participants, solution types, and industry interest, and will inform future industry engagements, acquisition planning, and assessment of potential use of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. 2.0 Forecasted Project(s) Overview The projects identified below represent current candidates for industrialized construction methodologies across multiple military installations. This listing is non-exhaustive and subject to change. Solutions deployed under this initiative may be adapted and scaled across additional facilities as future requirements are defined. Note: Projects may include secure spaces. Auto Multi-Purpose Machine Gun Range Construct a modified standard design Multipurpose Machine Gun (MPMG) Range at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Primary facilities include the MPMG Range, Range Control Tower, Range Operations and Storage Building, Range Classroom Building, Covered Mess, Ammunition Breakdown Building, Covered Bleacher, and building information systems. Supporting facilities include site improvements, paving, erosion control measures, electric service, and information systems. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life span of 40 years in accordance with Department of War�s (DoW) Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200-02), including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. Demolish 2 buildings at Fort Bragg, NC (459 Total ft2) LFSHX - Live Fire Exercise Shoothouse Construct standard design Live Fire Exercise Shoothouse. Primary facilities include the shoothouse, range operations control area, after action review building (small), operations/storage building (small), ammunition breakdown building, and latrine (aerated vault type). Supporting facilities include electric service, site improvements, and information systems. Access for persons with disabilities will be provided in the control and maintenance buildings. Air conditioning/heating: 4 tons. Supporting facilities cost is high due to the distance to the nearest utility hookups. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life span of 40 years in accordance with DoW's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200- 02) including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. 38RQS Guardian Angel Squadron Ops Construction of two new rescue squadron operations facilities, aircrew flight equipment facility, rescue maritime facility, open sided covered storage facility and an addition to the existing rescue squadron facility, building 663. Supporting facilities will include site preparations, site improvement, utilities, parking and walkways, landscaping, communications, allied support for modular buildings and all other work necessary for complete and usable facilities. Facility renovation of buildings 606 and 607 will include realignment of existing space, including work to interior walls, all utility/support systems including heating and cooling systems and fire detection and suppression systems. This Project also includes allied support construction for relocatable modular buildings to be used as swing space for the duration of construction, modular buildings include command and control, communication building, medical office, and portable armory unit. F35A Flight Simulator Construct a six-bay flight simulator facility for F-35A aircraft on Moody AFB. Facility will include space for 6 aircraft flight simulator bays, administration, records, classrooms, brief/debrief rooms, classified server room, and storage space for F-35A pilot flight simulator training. This facility will include Secure and Special Access Program spaces which must comply with the Intelligence Community Directive 705 criteria and standards. Supporting facilities will include demolition, site improvements, utilities, parking, and communications. F35A Precision Guided Munitions Construct Precision Guided Munition and Igloo Facilities at Moody AFB. Two Igloo facilities will be constructed with concrete headwall and precast, reinforced slabs on the top. Igloos are earth covered with earth fill surrounding the three closed sides with a 2:1 slide slope. The Igloo facilities will include motorized blast-proof steel doors, conduit infrastructure of Intrusion Detection System (IDS), lightning protection and grounding systems. Passive ventilation and floor drains are included for moisture. Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces shall comply with the Intelligence Community Directive 705 criteria and standards. Supporting facilities include utilities, access roads, pavement, parking, site improvements, communications infrastructure, signage, lighting, and unexploded ordnance clearance. F35A Consolidated AGE Support Facility Construct a new Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) consolidated facility to include administrative offices, parts storage, shop space, covered storage and open storage. This facility will include Secure and Special Access Program spaces which must comply with the Intelligence Community Directive 705 criteria and standards. Supporting facilities will include demolition, site improvements, landscaping, utilities, parking, and communications. F35A Egress Trainer Alter and renovate the internal space for the existing Field Training facility and construct an egress trainer. Alteration and renovation will include the addition of a bathroom and locker room, new carpet and paint, selective floor and ceiling replacement, and selective partition demolition. The addition will construct an attached egress trainer with a 21 feet ceiling height and a crane. Supporting facilities will include site improvements, utilities, and communications. 3.0 Requested Information & Market Intelligence Questionnaire Section - General Information Provide responses to the survey linked herein. https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/NX8GA8QFN5 Section - Capabilities Respondents are asked to structure Capability Statements to include the following elements: Corporate Overview - A brief summary of your firm's core capabilities, relevant experience, and capacity to perform the type of work contemplated under this RFI. Commercial Best Practices. To the extent available, provide information regarding commercial best practices applicable to the contemplated construction delivery method, including: Typical pricing/payment structures Geographic coverage Typical project schedule timelines, long lead ite

description: This scope of work is to rebuild and renovate the Kautz Road Substation (KRS), which is UIP subproject SP-2. The KRS supplies electricity to various lab buildings and systems. These systems serve both conventional facility needs, as well as process utility requirements. It is vital to Fermilab�s mission that KRS be revitalized and expanded, ensuring the ability to serve existing and future loads. The General contractor shall furnish all required supervision, labor, materials, tools, plant and appurtenances necessary to perform diligently and fully all work as described in the drawings and technical specifications. All work includes transportation, overhead, bonding costs, safety oversight, quality control oversight, and supervision as required to construct the project described in the drawings, technical specification and the detailed description contained herein. The critical schedule constraint for construction of this project is Fermilab�s accelerator shutdown, with an anticipated scheduled start on January 1, 2028, and anticipated end date of January 1, 2030- these dates may change depending on the needs of the Lab. description: RWP DUE DATE HAS BEEN EXTENDED TO 18 DECEMBER 2026 ___________________________ To: AEDC Velocity Alliance Consortium and Industry Partners via SAM.gov Project Title: Extreme Loads Tire Force Machine (ELTFM) Contracting Organization: AFTC/PZ (Arnold) Applicable NAICS Code: 334519 � Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing (Physical Properties Testing Equipment) Applicable PSC Code: 6635 � Physical Properties Testing and Inspection Equipment Acquisition Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 4022 � Other Transaction Authority for Prototypes Offerors may recommend an alternate NAICS or PSC code for consideration. The 704th Test Group (704 TG) Aerospace Survivability and Safety Office (OL-AC) at Wright- Patterson AFB, Ohio, requires an advanced, state-of-the-art testing capability to replace its legacy Tire Force Machine (TFM). Currently, the legacy system cannot meet the high vertical and lateral load requirements of current tire test profiles. To bridge this critical testing gap, the Government is initiating the Extreme Loads Tire Force Machine (ELTFM) prototype project. The ELTFM is conceived as a unique, high-capacity dynamic test machine designed to bridge the operational gap between high-speed dynamometer force testing and static load presses. See request for white paper attached for details. NOTE: The requirement documents for this effort are marked Distribution D and/or Export Controlled. For access to these documents, please provide your company's CAGE to the POCs listed. Once CMMC Level 2 (Self) and JCP certification are confirmed, the documents will be sent via DoD SAFE.

title: Pouch Converters Capable of Fabricating, Filling, Processing (via commercial sterilization) Group Sized Serving Pouches
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command - Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC) in identifying industrial sources and capabilities to fabricate, fill and process (via commercial sterilization) a Group Serving Pouch (GSP), which will be included in the U.S. military�s Group Ration Platform. The Government requests responders submit a Broad Other Transaction Authority Announcement (BOTAA) preproposal as outlined in DEVCOM-SC BOTAA 22-01 located at: https://sam.gov/opp/126eaf3a78d847f69b7c94b606877f92/view. Please refer to Topic Area of Interest �A. SOLDIER SUSTAINMENT DIRECTORATE (SSD)� starting on page 19. Submit the BOTAA preproposal to: Jean.m.trumpis.civ@army.mil and Danielle.l.froio-blumsack.civ@army.mil by December 18, 2026, by 5 PM EST. Description: DEVCOM-SC is requesting preproposals on industrial sources and relevant capabilities pertaining to pouch fabrication, filling and processing of vegetable-based food components for use in Group Rations. Specific Specifications: Capability to fabricate (or procure) GSPs, fill with vegetable and brine mixture, and commercially sterilize. Volumetric size of the GSP shall be between 24 to 144 ounces. Targeted shelf life of the pouch is 3 years at 80F Residual gas volume in the filled and sealed GSP shall not exceed 12% of the fill volume. The material used for the pouch shall be generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for use with food in accordance with 21 CFR, Parts 170-199 or other standards and regulations. The closure seal width shall be a minimum 1/8 inch for conventional heat seals or a minimum 1.0 mm for ultrasonic seals. The pouches shall be filled and hermetically sealed such that after thermal processing, the pouches shall withstand an internal pressure of 10 psig for 30 seconds, while the pouch is held between plates with a 2-inch distance between them. Pouches must pass a distribution testing sequence, which consists of drop and vibration testing Deliverables: All documentation submitted shall be submitted as MS Word, Adobe PDF, MS PowerPoint, Visio, or MS Excel files. Respondents: The White Paper should be written in respondent format, double spaced, and minimum font size of 10 pt. Paper should not exceed 12 pages, including cover. This paper should cover company information (company name, CAGE code, mailing address, and primary point of contact information (to include telephone number and email address). The paper should cover the 5 Ws, as applicable. (e.g., What, Where, When, Why and Who. Example focus areas: Please discuss any/all relevant current products and services that currently meet or will be able to meet the enclosed requirements Vendors are encouraged to propose alternative products that may be able to meet or exceed the requirements. As applicable, please discuss how your product(s) was implemented within industry/Government. Please discuss, as applicable, proposed hardware used as part of the solution. title: Netherlands – Engineering services – Ingenieursdiensten Ontwerp en Aanleg
description: Vitens is voornemens vier raamovereenkomsten te sluiten met ingenieursbureaus voor het leveren van ingenieursdiensten ten behoeve van de voorbereiding, uitwerking en realisatie van projecten voor de bovengrondse drinkwaterinfrastructuur van Vitens. De opdracht is primair gericht op het ondersteunen van de investeringsopgave van de afdeling Ontwerp en Aanleg (O&A). De dienstverlening omvat onder meer ontwerp en engineering van bovengrondse drinkwaterinfrastructuur en terreinleidingen, technisch management en projectbeheersing, kostenmanagement, ondersteuning bij de voorbereiding, uitwerking en realisatie van projecten en projectmatige ondersteuning bij de ontwikkeling en doorontwikkeling van asset- en uitvoeringsstandaarden. Daarnaast kan de dienstverlening worden ingezet voor specialistische technische ondersteuning bij calamiteiten of wanneer specifieke kennis van installaties, locaties of eerder gemaakte ontwerpkeuzes noodzakelijk is. De werkzaamheden richten zich in beginsel op ontwerp- en engineeringswerkzaamheden vanaf de definitiefase tot en met het voorlopig ontwerp. Afhankelijk van de aard, omvang en complexiteit van de opgave kan de dienstverlening worden uitgebreid tot en met het definitief ontwerp, het opstellen van bestekken en contractdocumenten en ondersteuning tijdens de realisatiefase. Vitens kiest voor een langdurig strategisch prestatiepartnerschap met vier ingenieursbureaus. Naast het leveren van ingenieurscapaciteit en specialistische expertise wordt van de contractpartners een actieve bijdrage verwacht aan kennisontwikkeling, kennisdeling, standaardisatie, innovatie, productiviteitsverbetering en continue verbetering van de kwaliteit, doorlooptijd en kosten van projecten. De raamovereenkomsten hebben een beoogde looptijd van acht jaar (2027-2035). De maximale opdrachtwaarde bedraagt op basis van de huidige investeringsprognoses € 60 miljoen over de beoogde contractperiode.

title: Netherlands – Electricity distribution and control apparatus – Levering, modernisering en onderhoud van frequentieregelaars
description: Vitens is voornemens twee raamovereenkomsten te sluiten voor de levering, installatie, modernisering, het onderhoud en de revisie van frequentieregelaars voor industrieel gebruik binnen haar drinkwaterproductie- en distributie-infrastructuur. De opdracht omvat de volledige levenscyclus van frequentieregelaars en bestaat onder meer uit engineering, selectie en dimensionering, levering van nieuwe frequentieregelaars en reserveonderdelen, installatie, parametrisering, inbedrijfstelling, preventief onderhoud, diagnose en technisch advies, reparatie, revisie, vervanging en verantwoorde uitfasering van bestaande frequentieregelaars. Een belangrijk onderdeel van de opdracht betreft de planmatige vervanging van frequentieregelaars die door de fabrikant End of Life zijn verklaard of gedurende de looptijd van de overeenkomst End of Life worden. Op basis van de huidige inzichten wordt rekening gehouden met de vervanging van circa 1.000 frequentieregelaars gedurende de maximale contractperiode van acht jaar. Daarnaast omvat de opdracht correctief onderhoud, waaronder reparaties, revisies en ongeplande vervangingen. De opdrachten worden gedurende de looptijd van de raamovereenkomsten hoofdzakelijk verstrekt via minicompetities tussen de twee opdrachtnemers. Dit geldt zowel voor preventief geplande vervangingen als voor onverwachte maar planbare werkzaamheden. Voor calamiteiten en spoedeisende werkzaamheden gelden aanvullende afspraken over de regionale inzet en beschikbaarheid van de opdrachtnemers. De beoogde looptijd van de raamovereenkomsten bedraagt vier jaar, met twee opties tot verlenging van elk twee jaar. De totale geraamde waarde van de opdracht bedraagt maximaal € 14 miljoen exclusief btw over de maximale contractperiode van acht jaar.

Options (not evaluated): "Projects and project costs" and "Integrated web shop".

title: Polymerer til Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S
description: Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S inviterer ansøgere til at byde på nærværende 4-årige rammeaftale på levering af polymerer til afvanding af spildevandsslam på Ordregivers renseanlæg. En forudsætning for at kunne afgive tilbud - og dermed deltage i udbuddets tilbuds- og forhandlingsfase er, at virksomheden har ansøgt om at blive prækvalificeret, og at Ordregiver har vurderet, at virksomheden er egnet. Ordregiver vil herefter opfordre tilbudsgivere til at afgive tilbud i tilbudsfasen. Der er direkte adgang til udbudsmaterialet på udbudsportalen Comdia. Her vil spørgsmål/svar og tilrettede dokumenter ligeledes være tilgængelige. Ansøger er selv ansvarlig for, at ansøgningen lever op til alle krav og betingelser i udbudsmaterialet, og Ansøger bør være opmærksom på, at eventuelle uklarheder i oplysninger i Ansøgers tilbud kan tillægges negativ vægt ved vurdering af Ansøgers egnethed eller evaluering af tilbuddet. Rammeaftalen består i transport (levering) af polymerer til forafvanding og slutafvanding af spildevandsslam på de herunder beskrevne renseanlæg: Delaftale 1: •Skagen Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Skagen Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Ålbæk Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) Delaftale 2: •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Sæby Renseanlæg (forafvanding) Delaftale 3: •Forrens GEM (flotation) Ordregiver ønsker at opnå et højt tørstof i det slutafvandede slam i kombination med tilfredsstillende rejektvandskvalitet og et lavt specifikt polymerforbrug. For yderligere specifikationer for de enkelte renseanlæg henvises der til Bilag 1 Kravspecifikation og Bilag 1A Fotografisk beskrivelse af slamafvandingsanlæg. Rammeaftalens forventede indkøbt polymermængde antages at blive: Delaftale 1: 193.200 kg Delaftale 2: 155.200 kg Delaftale 3: 58.000 kg Rammeaftalens maksimale indkøbt polymermængde udgør: Delaftale 1: 240.000 kg. Delaftale 2: 170.000 kg. Delaftale 3: 90.000 kg. Det er væsentligt at bemærke, at forbruget af polymer på Delaftale 1 og 3 i praksis afhænger meget af den modtagne mængde spildevand fra fiskeindustrien, hvorfor polymerforbruget her kan variere meget fra år til år. Dette er søgt indregnet i de stipulerede maksimale polymermængder. Det forventede årlige estimat udgør alene estimater, som ikke er bindende for Ordregiver. Dette betyder, at Ordregiver ikke forpligter sig ud over sit faktiske forbrug, som løbende kan ændre sig som følge af ændring af slammets egenskaber og løbende tildelinger baseret på afholdte tests jf. rammeaftalens proces for tildelinger af rekvisitioner. Ansøger vil således ikke være berettiget til positiv opfyldelsesinteresse eller på anden måde godtgørelse, hvis Ordregivers forbrug skulle ligge under det anførte estimat eller under Ansøgers forventninger. Ordregiver forventer at prækvalificere 5 ansøgere til deltagelse i tilbudsfasen. På baggrund af evalueringen af de indkomne tilbud i tilbudsfasen, forventer Ordregiver at indgå rammeaftale med to tilbudsgivere for hver delaftale. Såfremt der er flere ansøgere, der ikke er omfattet af én eller flere af udelukkelsesgrundene, og som opfylder minimumskravene til egnethedskriterierne, end ovenstående antal af tilbudsgivere, vil udvælgelsen af de ansøgere, der gives mulighed for at afgive tilbud, ske ud fra følgende kriterier: A.CV på tilbudte kontaktperson (kundeansvarlig) (50% vægtning) -Erfaring -Uddannelse B.Referencer jf. afsnit 11.2 i prækvalifikationsbetingelserne (50 % vægtning) -Sammenlignelige referencer med fokus på levering af polymerer til renseanlæg af tilsvarende størrelse Ansøger skal vedlægge særskilt CV for den tilbudte kontaktperson. CV må maksimalt fylde 1 A4-side (2400 tegn). Blandt de ansøgere, der opfylder minimumskravene til egnethed, foretager Ordregiver en vurdering af modtagne CV og referencerne under hvert vurderingstema. Vurderingen angår alene CV og referencernes relevans og styrke i forhold til den udbudte opgave og anvendes til at rangordne de egnede ansøgere. Under hvert vurderingstema tildeler Ordregiver en karakter fra 0 til 5. Karakteren for hvert vurderingstema multipliceres med temaets vægtning. De vægtede karakterer sammenlægges til en samlet score på maksimalt 6,00 point. Ansøgerne rangeres herefter efter deres samlede score. De ansøgere, der opnår de højeste samlede scorer, udvælges til at afgive tilbud. Såfremt to eller flere ansøgere opnår samme samlede score, rangeres ansøgerne efter deres score under vurderingstema A. Udvælgelsen foretages på grundlag af de oplysninger, som fremgår af Ansøgernes referencer. Det er Ansøgerens ansvar at beskrive referencerne tilstrækkeligt detaljeret til, at Ordregiver kan vurdere referencernes relevans og omfang i forhold til de enkelte vurderingstemaer. Yderligere beskrivelse af evalueringsmodel for udvælgelse af ansøgere fremgår af prækvalifikationsbetingelserne afsnit 12.

description: Pfaffenwaldring 57, 70569 Stuttgart, Universität Stuttgart; NWZ II, Sanierung für Chemie, Fachplanungsleistungen für Technische Ausrüstung nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI, Anlagengruppen 4 und 5, Das Naturwissenschaftliche Zentrum (NWZ) I und II im Pfaffenwaldring (PWR) 55 und 57 in Stuttgart wurde in den 1970er Jahren fertiggestellt. Das NWZ soll in den kommenden Jahren abschnittsweise saniert werden. Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Planungsleistungen sind die elektrotechnischen Vorabmaßnahmen im NWZ I, die im Vorgriff auf die geplante Sanierung des NWZ II im ersten Sanierungsabschnitt erforderlich werden. Die Maßnahmen sind Bestandteil der Gesamtsanierungsmaßnahme NWZ. Im Zuge der Sanierung des NWZ II müssen bestehende Versorgungs- und technische Anlagen zwischen NWZ I und NWZ II getrennt, angepasst oder neu hergestellt werden. Darüber hinaus müssen bisher im NWZ II untergebrachte Nutzungen während der Sanierung interimsweise in das NWZ I verlagert werden. Hierfür sind die vorhandenen technischen Anlagen in den betreffenden Bereichen zu ertüchtigen bzw. vollständig neu aufzubauen. Gleichzeitig werden bestehende Nutzungen, insbesondere die Bibliothek, innerhalb des NWZ I verdichtet und neu organisiert. Im Laborhochhaus mit den angrenzenden Flachbauten des NWZ I ist im Wesentlichen die Fakultät Chemie untergebracht. In den Flachbauten befinden sich unter anderem Hörsäle, die Universitätsbibliothek und eine Cafeteria. Das NWZ I verfügt über insgesamt ca. 23.800 m² NUF (1-6). Die zur Bearbeitung vorgesehenen Bereiche umfassen insgesamt ca. 2.900 m² NUF und betreffen im Wesentlichen: die Neuordnung und Verdichtung der Universitätsbibliothek mit ca. 2.520 m² NUF, Verwaltungs- und Fachschaftsflächen mit ca. 90 m² NUF sowie Praktikums- und Laborflächen mit ca. 290 m² NUF. Aufgrund der erforderlichen Neuorganisation der Flucht- und Rettungswege sind zudem elektrotechnische Anlagen für temporäre Flucht- und Rettungswege zu planen. Hierzu gehören insbesondere die Beleuchtung und erforderliche Sicherheitsbeleuchtung der vorgesehenen Interims- Treppenhäuser einschließlich der Fluchtwege bis zu den Sammelplätzen. Die elektrotechnische Planung hat außerdem die Anpassung der Brandmeldeanlage an die veränderte Gebäudestruktur und die vorgesehenen Bauabschnitte zu berücksichtigen. Dies betrifft insbesondere die Abtrennung der Gebäudeteile, den Rückbau bzw. die Anpassung bestehender Melder und Leitungswege sowie erforderliche Interimslösungen während der Bauphase. Im Bereich der Bibliothek sind insbesondere die Beleuchtungsanlage, Stromversorgung, LAN-Verkabelung und WLAN-Infrastruktur an die zukünftige Nutzung und die geplante Nachverdichtung anzupassen. Für die in das NWZ I zu verlagernden Praktikums- und Laborflächen sind die elektrotechnischen Anlagen entsprechend den zukünftigen Nutzeranforderungen neu zu planen. Dies umfasst insbesondere die 230/ 400-V-Stromversorgung, Unterverteilungen, Endstromkreise, Beleuchtung, LAN-Verkabelung sowie die erforderlichen Anschlüsse für die technische Laborausstattung. Das Gebäude befindet sich größtenteils im Errichtungszustand und weist entsprechende bauzeitliche Schadstoffbelastungen auf. Die Umsetzung der Maßnahme erfolgt bei laufendem Universitäts- und Gebäudebetrieb. Die Aufrechterhaltung der Versorgung und des Betriebs der nicht von den jeweiligen Bauabschnitten betroffenen Bereiche ist während der gesamten Maßnahme sicherzustellen. Die Baukosten der Kostengruppen 440-450 betragen nach derzeitiger Kostenschätzung ca. 1.100.000 Euro. Der Projektstart ist mit der Auftragserteilung Anfang März 2027 vorgesehen. Die Fertigstellung der Maßnahme ist für das 1. Quartal 2031 vorgesehen. Beabsichtigt ist die Beauftragung von Fachplanungsleistungen nach Teil 4, Abschnitt 2 HOAI für die folgende zur Technischen Ausrüstung gehören Anlagengruppe nach § 53 Absatz 2 HOAI: Nr. 4 Starkstromanlagen und Nr. 5 Fernmelde- und informationstechnische Anlagen, Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 2 , 3 und 5 bis 8 sowie Besondere Leistungen.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Realisierungswettbewerb „Neubau Feuer- und Rettungswache“ in Lippstadt
description: Der derzeitige Standort der Feuer- und Rettungswache Lippstadt weist im Brandschutzbedarfsplan zahlreiche Mängel auf, u. a. das Fehlen von ausreichenden Flächen in verschiedenen Funktionsbereichen, die Unterbringungssituation für das Personal sowie die ungünstige Alarmausfahrten für Großfahrzeuge und stellt somit keine Zukunftsperspektive dar. Der politisch beschlossene neue Standort auf dem Uniongelände im Lippstädter Stadtgebiet bietet hinsichtlich der Erreichbarkeit für die ehrenamtlichen Einsatzkräfte und die größtmögliche Flächenabdeckung und kürzeste Eintreffzeit aus Sicht des Hauptamtes geeignete Voraussetzungen. Der zu errichtende Neubau der weiterhin kombinierten Feuer- und Rettungswache Lippstadt mit hauptamtlichen Kräften soll auf dem südlichen Bereich des Uniongeländes zukunftsfähig die notwendigen Arbeitsbedingungen für das hauptberufliche Einsatzpersonal Brandschutz und Rettungsdienst sowie die ehrenamtlichen Einsatzkräfte sicherstellen, um bei Notlagen jeglicher Art die entsprechende Hilfeleistung zu gewährleisten. Das gesamte Raumprogramm umfasst ein Flächensoll von ca. 7.850 m² zzgl. entwurfsabhängiger Flächen, das in Summe 46 Stellplätze in den Fahrzeughallen und die Waschhalle beinhaltet. Ziel des Wettbewerbes ist es, über alternative und optimierte Konzepte, die den unterschiedlichen Anforderungen in gleicher Weise gerecht werden, ein/e geeignete/n AuftragnehmerIn (ArchitektIn) für die weiteren Planungsleistungen zu finden.

title: Denmark – Chemical products – Polymerer til Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S
description: Frederikshavn Forsyning A/S inviterer ansøgere til at byde på nærværende 4-årige rammeaftale på levering af polymerer til afvanding af spildevandsslam på Ordregivers renseanlæg. En forudsætning for at kunne afgive tilbud - og dermed deltage i udbuddets tilbuds- og forhandlingsfase er, at virksomheden har ansøgt om at blive prækvalificeret, og at Ordregiver har vurderet, at virksomheden er egnet. Ordregiver vil herefter opfordre tilbudsgivere til at afgive tilbud i tilbudsfasen. Der er direkte adgang til udbudsmaterialet på udbudsportalen Comdia. Her vil spørgsmål/svar og tilrettede dokumenter ligeledes være tilgængelige. Ansøger er selv ansvarlig for, at ansøgningen lever op til alle krav og betingelser i udbudsmaterialet, og Ansøger bør være opmærksom på, at eventuelle uklarheder i oplysninger i Ansøgers tilbud kan tillægges negativ vægt ved vurdering af Ansøgers egnethed eller evaluering af tilbuddet. Rammeaftalen består i transport (levering) af polymerer til forafvanding og slutafvanding af spildevandsslam på de herunder beskrevne renseanlæg: Delaftale 1: •Skagen Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Skagen Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Ålbæk Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) Delaftale 2: •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (forafvanding) •Frederikshavn Renseanlæg (slutafvanding) •Sæby Renseanlæg (forafvanding) Delaftale 3: •Forrens GEM (flotation) Ordregiver ønsker at opnå et højt tørstof i det slutafvandede slam i kombination med tilfredsstillende rejektvandskvalitet og et lavt specifikt polymerforbrug. For yderligere specifikationer for de enkelte renseanlæg henvises der til Bilag 1 Kravspecifikation og Bilag 1A Fotografisk beskrivelse af slamafvandingsanlæg. Rammeaftalens forventede indkøbt polymermængde antages at blive: Delaftale 1: 193.200 kg Delaftale 2: 155.200 kg Delaftale 3: 58.000 kg Rammeaftalens maksimale indkøbt polymermængde udgør: Delaftale 1: 240.000 kg. Delaftale 2: 170.000 kg. Delaftale 3: 90.000 kg. Det er væsentligt at bemærke, at forbruget af polymer på Delaftale 1 og 3 i praksis afhænger meget af den modtagne mængde spildevand fra fiskeindustrien, hvorfor polymerforbruget her kan variere meget fra år til år. Dette er søgt indregnet i de stipulerede maksimale polymermængder. Det forventede årlige estimat udgør alene estimater, som ikke er bindende for Ordregiver. Dette betyder, at Ordregiver ikke forpligter sig ud over sit faktiske forbrug, som løbende kan ændre sig som følge af ændring af slammets egenskaber og løbende tildelinger baseret på afholdte tests jf. rammeaftalens proces for tildelinger af rekvisitioner. Ansøger vil således ikke være berettiget til positiv opfyldelsesinteresse eller på anden måde godtgørelse, hvis Ordregivers forbrug skulle ligge under det anførte estimat eller under Ansøgers forventninger. Ordregiver forventer at prækvalificere 5 ansøgere til deltagelse i tilbudsfasen. På baggrund af evalueringen af de indkomne tilbud i tilbudsfasen, forventer Ordregiver at indgå rammeaftale med to tilbudsgivere for hver delaftale. Såfremt der er flere ansøgere, der ikke er omfattet af én eller flere af udelukkelsesgrundene, og som opfylder minimumskravene til egnethedskriterierne, end ovenstående antal af tilbudsgivere, vil udvælgelsen af de ansøgere, der gives mulighed for at afgive tilbud, ske ud fra følgende kriterier: A.CV på tilbudte kontaktperson (kundeansvarlig) (50% vægtning) -Erfaring -Uddannelse B.Referencer jf. afsnit 11.2 i prækvalifikationsbetingelserne (50 % vægtning) -Sammenlignelige referencer med fokus på levering af polymerer til renseanlæg af tilsvarende størrelse Ansøger skal vedlægge særskilt CV for den tilbudte kontaktperson. CV må maksimalt fylde 1 A4-side (2400 tegn). Blandt de ansøgere, der opfylder minimumskravene til egnethed, foretager Ordregiver en vurdering af modtagne CV og referencerne under hvert vurderingstema. Vurderingen angår alene CV og referencernes relevans og styrke i forhold til den udbudte opgave og anvendes til at rangordne de egnede ansøgere. Under hvert vurderingstema tildeler Ordregiver en karakter fra 0 til 5. Karakteren for hvert vurderingstema multipliceres med temaets vægtning. De vægtede karakterer sammenlægges til en samlet score på maksimalt 6,00 point. Ansøgerne rangeres herefter efter deres samlede score. De ansøgere, der opnår de højeste samlede scorer, udvælges til at afgive tilbud. Såfremt to eller flere ansøgere opnår samme samlede score, rangeres ansøgerne efter deres score under vurderingstema A. Udvælgelsen foretages på grundlag af de oplysninger, som fremgår af Ansøgernes referencer. Det er Ansøgerens ansvar at beskrive referencerne tilstrækkeligt detaljeret til, at Ordregiver kan vurdere referencernes relevans og omfang i forhold til de enkelte vurderingstemaer. Yderligere beskrivelse af evalueringsmodel for udvælgelse af ansøgere fremgår af prækvalifikationsbetingelserne afsnit 12.

Weiterhin sind die Demontage und Entsorgung der alten Technik vorgesehen. Die Umsetzung der Ausführung muss eine einfache Bedienbarkeit zur Durchführung verschiedenartiger Veranstaltungsformen ermöglichen. Ziel der Maßnahme ist die Erneuerung der bestehenden Bildwiedergabetechnik unter Berücksichtigung der vorhandenen baulichen, mechanischen und medientechnischen Randbedingungen. Hierzu muss seitens des zu beauftragenden Unternehmens ein Konzept zur Umsetzung der Leistungen erstellt werden.

title: Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services Solicitation
description: *This Solicitation is for SEAPORT NXG MAC HOLDERS ONLY. No other offers will be considered. Seaport MAC Holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to submit offers.*Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) Division Keyport is soliciting a task order for Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services (KISSS). This requirement supports the Infrastructure Services Division (Code 102) and the Security Division (Code 105).The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Safety Compliance, Environmental Compliance, Facilities Engineering, Facilities Planning, Facilities Management, Facilities Maintenance, Security Operations Support, and Monitoring Support. The selected contractor will support Code 102 in its mission to plan, manage, and maintain NUWC Division Keyports safety, environmental, and facilities programs, while also providing security services under the direction of the Code 105 Security Office. The contemplated task order will be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) under the SeaPort NxG allowing any small business company in SeaPort to propose. It will be awarded on a best value basis to the Government. A trade-off analysis will be carried out, taking into consideration technical capability, past performance, and cost/price. It will include a base period of twelve (12) months and may include up to four (4) option years. The solicitation is set aside for Seaport Small businesses. The applicable PSC code for this requirement is R499 and the applicable NAICS code is 541330. The task order is predicted to be awarded in November 2027 with a predicted start date of January 2028. The support services are currently being performed under SeaPort-NxG task order N0025322F3001 by McLaughlin Research Corporation.

title: USACE Moorings Life Safety Improvement Project
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT and is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER FAR SUBPART 5.2. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the Government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: TBD. The approximate value of Project will be $5 to $25M. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � before 3:00 pm Pacific on December 18th 2026. 1. Project Details and Background The project is to upgrade the administration buildings at the US Government Moorings located on the west bank of the Willamette River (River Miles 6.08 to 6.21). This facility serves as the primary port, repair and supply base for the USACE Portland District Fleet, including dredges and hydro survey vessels. After a major fire at the facility, the Government is pursuing life safety and seismic upgrades to the facility. 2. Project Scope This project will involve upgrading the Fire Protection systems to the Administration building, Machine Shop, Warehouse, Weld Shop, and sprinkler system to the Administration building and Weld shop and adding site lighting. This would also include life safety and code improvements within the same buildings. Anticipated Construction Schedule: CENWP intends to advertise in May 2027 and award in July 2027. Construction Contract with estimated construction completion by the end of calendar year 2028. Estimated Construction Cost (ECC): The current ECC is between $5,000,000 to $25,000,000 Number and Type of Contracts: NWP contemplates awarding one (1), Firm Fixed-Price contract. The acquisition strategy decision has not yet been determined. Maximum small business participation is being sought at both the Prime and subcontracting levels. Anticipated Source Selection Process: The expected method to determine the best value to the government is Invitation for Bid. Project Details: The following information represents the project objectives: Improve the life safety of the facilities at the US. Government Moorings. 3. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically by e-mail to SUBJECT: US Moorings Life Safety Upgrade to Ian Lutjens at Ian.k.Lutjens@usarmy.mil and Brandon Lasich at Brandon.M.Lasich@usace.army.mil Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to six (6) pages and shall include the following information: Experience in installing fire control systems. Experience in installing Sprinkler systems. Retro fitting new health life safety systems into an older building. Upgrading utilities in an older building 4. Disclaimer and Important Notes. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov to have size status considered. You must remain current for the duration of the source selection process to be eligible for award of a Government contract.

title: Request for Information (RFI) - Commercial Loan Servicing and Asset Administration Services
description: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Division of Resolutions and Receiverships (DRR), is conducting market research to identify qualified firms capable of providing commercial loan and asset servicing, administration, and resolution support services for large-volume domestic portfolios. Services may involve portfolios exceeding 10,000 assets and approximately $25 billion in aggregate book value. The FDIC is particularly interested in industry's ability to rapidly assume servicing responsibility for complex commercial loan portfolios, including portfolios associated with failed financial institutions, bridge banks, receiverships, and other resolution-related environments. Portfolios may include Commercial Real Estate (CRE), Commercial and Industrial (C&I), Acquisition, Development, and Construction (ADC), agricultural, government-guaranteed, syndicated and participation loans, specialty banking assets, servicing rights, securitized assets, ORE/REO assets, and performing, delinquent, non-performing, or matured loans. Services may include portfolio onboarding and transfer, loan administration, payment processing, collections, workout and restructuring activities, collateral management, foreclosure and liquidation support, asset disposition support, reporting, and related servicing functions. Interested parties are requested to complete and submit (Appendix A) �RFI LBS � Commercial� as their primary response. Respondents may also provide supplemental capability information. The FDIC strongly encourages use of the Appendix A template to facilitate efficient and consistent market research analysis. The FDIC is particularly interested in information regarding: Servicing capacity and scalability Portfolio transfer and onboarding experience Government-guaranteed loan servicing experience Receivership, resolution, workout, and asset disposition experience Cybersecurity capabilities Recommended contract structures and performance metrics Industry best practices and risk considerations Responses are encouraged from commercial loan servicers, financial institutions, specialty servicers, asset managers, and other organizations with relevant experience and capabilities. DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and information-gathering purposes. This notice does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or a commitment by the FDIC to award a contract. Responses will be used solely to support acquisition planning and assess industry capabilities. The FDIC will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response to this notice.

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor/Hickam, Hawaii intends to award Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Multiple Award Contract (MAC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to provide marine resource technical services throughout the Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC) Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas worldwide as needed. This solicitation will be issued as an unrestricted procurement with a partial small business set-aside that will result in the award of multiple award contracts that are comprised of two major divisions. The resulting multiple award contracts will be comprised of two major divisions: An Unrestricted Division and a partial Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division. The work shall be located primarily in Hawaii, Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). The Government may also require marine resource technical services throughout the NAVFAC Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), and other areas in the NAVFAC AOR worldwide as needed. All Marine Resource Technical Services conducted under the resultant contracts shall conform to the statutes, regulations, instructions and guidelines in compliance with the Request for Proposal (RFP). The resulting contract will include requirements that include but are not limited to, the following: (1) Coordination of Monitoring Projects and Subject Matter Experts, (2) Data Management, (3) Analysis and Reporting, (4) Visual Surveys, (5) Diving and Marine Resource Surveys, (6) Marine Species Observers, (7) Passive Acoustic Monitoring, (8) Marine Species Tagging and Tracking, (9) Photo Identification, (10) Behavioral Studies, (11) Habitat Restoration, (12) Coral Translocation, (13) Anomaly Avoidance Surveys, (14) Event Reconstruction and Environmental Data Integration, (15) Ecological Analysis, (16) Outreach, (17) Miscellaneous Marine Biological Resource Services, (18) Biomonitoring, (19) Biosecurity and Aquatic Invasive Species Management, (20) Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMPs), (21) NEPA, Environmental Planning and Supporting Studies, (22) GIS Mapping, (23) Endangered Species Act (ESA) Biological Opinions, (24) Magnuson Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA) Essential Fish Habitat (EFH) Assessments, and (25) Marine Mammal Protection Act. Work will be performed in accordance with the requirements of the Performance Work Statement, and may involve regulatory compliance, planning, analyzing, and various related services on any one or a combination of more than one task order. Exact location of each effort will be designated on individual Task Orders. The entire term of the contract is a maximum of $99 million or 90 months (consisting of a 12-month base period, six (6) 12-month option periods and one (1) 6-month extension of services period), whichever occurs first. Task orders will typically range between $3,500 and $10,000,000. Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. The Government makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, during the term of the contract, a minimum of $5,000 is guaranteed for each awardee under the contract. As task orders are awarded that exceed the $5,000, the $5,000 minimum guarantee will be deobligated and the Governments obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Projects competed to the unrestricted division will require a minimum of 18% of the work to be subcontracted to small businesses. Approximately $68.5M will be work performed in the NAVFAC Pacific Area of Responsibility (AOR), $15M in the NAVFAC Hawaii AOR and $15.5M in the NAVFAC Marianas AOR. These amounts may fluctuate with the potential need for the different types of specific services listed above and whether adequate competition exists within the SBSA Division and those contractors are capable of successfully executing those services. If one or no SBSA Division contractors submit a proposal in response to a task order request for proposal (RFP), the Contracting Officer may compete the task order amongst the Unrestricted Division contractors. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541990 All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services and the corresponding small business size standard is $19.5 million (which will determine eligibility for awards under the Small Business Set Aside (SBSA) Division). A MAC is a contract awarded from a single solicitation and may result in award to multiple contractors. This procurement consists of one solicitation with the intent to award no more than six (6) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type service contracts to the offerors whose proposals, conforming to the solicitation, represents the most advantageous offers to the Government resulting in the best value, price and non-price factors considered. The Government reserves the right to award more than six (6) contracts if it is determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Successful awardees will compete for future work during the term of the contract. This is a best value, trade off procurement. The Government intends to evaluate proposals without conducting discussions with any Offeror, except for clarifications as described in FAR 15.306(a). However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions with Offerors, if required. The non-price evaluation factors will be 1) Experience; 2) Sample Project; 3) Safety; 4) Small Business Utilization and Participation; and 5) Past Performance. Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are considered of equal importance to each other, and when combined, are equal in importance to the past performance evaluation Factor 5. When the proposal is evaluated as a whole, the technical factors and past performance factor combined are significantly more important than price. The evaluation of the Price Factor will be based on the sample project attached to the solicitation. The sample project is for evaluation purposes only and will not be awarded on the contract.

title: Enterprise Wide IT Support Services
description: The Department of the Navy, NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk, Philadelphia Office, on behalf of the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI), intends to solicit and award a task order for full-spectrum lifecycle Enterprise-Wide Information Technology (EWIT) Support Services. This posting serves as the formal public notification of the Government's Notice of Intent to Consolidate and Substantially Bundle Requirements in accordance with FAR 7.107-5 and DFARS 205.205-70. The prospective acquisition consolidates ten (10) active legacy task orders into a single, comprehensive task order. 2. Scope of Services To operate, maintain, secure, modernize, integrate, and enhance enterprise IT capabilities supporting mission operations, the Contractor will perform work across the following defined service domains: Enterprise Architecture, Assessment, Verification, and Transition: Architecture, technical assessment, independent verification, configuration-baseline, operational-readiness, transition, and technical analysis activities. IT Systems Engineering, Operations, and Sustainment: Engineering, operations, sustainment, modernization, migration, integration, and optimization support for designated IT systems and services. This includes cloud and hybrid-environment engineering, tenant/workload onboarding, infrastructure, backup/recovery, DevSecOps implementation, and identity/access security tool integration. Application Development and Sustainment: Development, modernization, sustainment, integration, migration, deployment, enhancement, and decommissioning of designated mission and business applications using commercial, Government, open-source, cloud-native, and traditional computing technologies. Data Services: Data-management, data-platform, data-engineering, data-science, analytics, automation, super-intelligence/machine-learning, visualization, and secure data-transport support. Cybersecurity Services: Cybersecurity engineering, compliance, authorization-support, assessment, remediation, monitoring, and incident-support services (including Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle support and authorization artifact development). Program, Service Management, and Transition: Program and service-management support directly associated with performance, including contract-management planning, schedule/risk/dependency tracking, configuration/change control, and transition-in/transition-out support. 3. Cloud Architecture: The operational environment utilizes industry-standard cloud service provider infrastructure, platform, and serverless capabilities at various impact and classification levels. Personnel Security Requirements: The anticipated effort requires a fully cleared workforce meeting Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility and access requirements at contract start for positions requiring such access. 4. title: TECHNOLOGY/BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY: A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers
description: Opportunity: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), operated by the Lawrence Livermore National Security (LLNS), LLC under contract no. DE-AC52-07NA27344 (Contract 44) with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is offering the opportunity to enter into a collaboration to further develop and commercialize its A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers. Background: Among the lowest-hanging fruits for improving the wall-plug efficiency (and therefore economic viability) and increasing the throughput of the EUV process is improving either the wall-plug efficiency of the EUV laser source itself or improving the laser-to-EUV conversion efficiency using optimized pulse shapes. The current state-of-the-art uses discharge-driven carbon dioxide lasers operating at 10.6 micron to hit the target (tin droplet) with one or more pre-pulses to flatten the droplet in the direction of laser propagation, followed by a high-energy (~ 1 J) main pulse to produce EUV. Description: This MOPA invention is primarily to seed a Tm:YLF laser chain that will amplify the laser pulses up to the ~ 1 J level for EUV generation. The arbitrary pulse shaping capability will be used to optimize EUV generation efficiency. The proposed laser front end will also be capable of precompensating for square pulse distortion in high-energy (> 100 J) Tm:YLF or Tm:YAG lasers. Additional applications spaces include seeding lasers (all-fiber or solid state) for medical devices (laser-assisted surgery), laser drilling, LIDAR, and standoff detection. Advantages/Benefits: The arbitrary pulse shaping capability allows tailoring of the laser pulse shape on timescales ranging from 100 ps to milliseconds, a capability that can be used to tune the pulse shape to increase the efficiency of EUV generation or radiation generation using other target materials besides tin. Potential Applications: EUV Sources lasers, additional applications spaces include seeding lasers (all-fiber or solid state) for medical devices (laser-assisted surgery), laser drilling, LIDAR, and standoff detection. Development Status: Current stage of technology development: TRL ? 0-2 ? 3-5 ? 5-9 LLNL is seeking industry partners with a demonstrated ability to bring such inventions to the market. Moving critical technology beyond the Laboratory to the commercial world helps our licensees gain a competitive edge in the marketplace. All licensing activities are conducted under policies relating to the strict nondisclosure of company proprietary information. Please visit the IPO website at https://ipo.llnl.gov/resources for more information on working with LLNL and the industrial partnering and technology transfer process. Note: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT. Companies interested in commercializing LLNL's A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers should provide an electronic OR written statement of interest, which includes the following: Company Name and address. The name, address, and telephone number of a point of contact. A description of corporate expertise and/or facilities relevant to commercializing this technology. Please provide a complete electronic OR written statement to ensure consideration of your interest in LLNL's A MOPA Fiber Laser Platform for Solid-State Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Driver Lasers. The subject heading in an email response should include the Notice ID and/or the title of LLNL�s Technology/Business Opportunity and directed to the Primary and Secondary Point of Contacts listed below. Construction practices shall comply with all VA solicitation drawings and specifications, VA regulations, procedures, and conditions for work at the medical center and any applicable codes as per requirements of all governing agencies. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System
description: The Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System from Los Alamos National Laboratory, transforms the heat pipes inside an alkali metal-cooled nuclear reactor from passive thermal conduits into active, sensor-driven fire defense components, giving designers of advanced small and microreactors a layered, automated safeguard against one of the most challenging hazards in their systems. By combining an inert gas buffer, a phase change material jacket, automated suppressant injection at multiple points and optional neutron-absorber dispersion into the reactor core, the system delivers redundant protection that responds within milliseconds of detecting fire-like conditions. This system enables advanced reactor developers to meet stringent safety expectations for remote, unattended and space-constrained deployments without redesigning the core architecture around bulky external suppression equipment. How it Works During normal operation, each heat pipe carries thermal energy away from the reactor core through the evaporation and condensation of an alkali metal working fluid, while valves connecting the heat pipe to external suppressant chambers remain closed. Temperature and pressure sensors continuously monitor the heat pipe reactor core and the valves near each heat pipe end, feeding data to a controller that compares readings against predefined thresholds. When a reading crosses the first threshold, the controller opens a valve and forces a fire suppressant material, typically a boron compound, into the interior of the heat pipe. If conditions worsen and a second threshold is crossed, additional valves activate to inject suppressant from the opposite end of the heat pipe, evacuate the working fluid through a dedicated valve and release suppressant into an inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe at the heat exchanger interface. Technical Description The system architecture centers on a heat pipe reactor core engaging a plurality of dual-ended or single-ended heat pipes, where both ends of each heat pipe extend externally of the core block so that suppressant can be introduced from either side of the core. A heat exchanger device sits at the heat rejection end of each heat pipe and defines an enclosed inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe, creating a physical gap between the alkali metal working fluid and any water-based cooling fluid. The chamber adds a second point of failure that must occur before incompatible fluids can interact, and the inert gas itself can serve as a blanketing agent for active flames. A layer of phase change material, typically a salt that doubles as a Class D fire extinguishing agent and alkali metal fire retardant, is disposed on the outer surface of the gas chamber, partitioned by fin-bearing components that both store thermal energy and improve heat transfer to the surrounding cooling fluid. The active suppression and shutdown logic is governed by a controller comprising memory, processor, input/output circuitry and communications circuitry, optionally implemented as a distributed or cloud-based system. First and second valves regulate suppressant flow into each end of the heat pipe interior cavity from dedicated suppressant chambers, while third and fourth valves regulate suppressant flow into the inert gas chamber from separate chambers. The second valve at the heat pipe�s far end can also be configured to evacuate working fluid either simultaneously with or prior to suppressant injection, encouraging dispersion of the suppressant throughout the pipe. As an additional shutdown pathway, the reactor core block can include gaps between fuel rods and heat pipes in which a neutron absorber material such as cadmium or a boron compound is preloaded; on detection of an alkali metal fire, the controller can release that absorber into the gaps to reduce core reactivity and aid shutdown, providing a coupled fire-and-reactivity response unique to this design. Advantages Multiple independent barriers between reactive alkali metals and potential ignition sources, reducing the probability of a single-point failure Automated, sensor-driven response that opens valves and injects suppressant within milliseconds of fire-like conditions being detected Dual-purpose phase change jacket that stores thermal energy during normal operation and acts as a fire retardant during an event Coupled fire suppression and reactor shutdown through optional neutron absorber dispersion into the core Flexible architecture compatible with both heat pipe-cooled reactor cores and auxiliary equipment such as molten salt pumps Configurable suppressant choices and threshold logic, allowing developers to tailor the response to their specific reactor design Market Applications Nuclear Energy (microreactors, small modular reactors, heat pipe-cooled designs) Power Generation (remote bases, mining sites, Arctic installations) Space and Lunar Surface Power (radioisotope and fission surface power systems) Industrial Process Heat (high-temperature manufacturing, hydrogen production facilities) Marine and Naval Propulsion (advanced compact reactor concepts for maritime use) Nuclear Safety Instrumentation (sensor and controller subsystems for licensed reactor operators) Development Status: TRL 3 U.S. Patent No. 12,640,276 LA-UR-26-25100 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. title: Spain – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Suministro, instalación y puesta en funcionamiento de un crío-ultramicrotomo para trabajar a temperatura ambiente y en condiciones criogénicas, junto con un procesador automático de tejidos, así como un criostato.
description: El objeto del contrato es el suministro, la instalación y la puesta en funcionamiento de equipamiento científico-técnico para la preparación y seccionamiento de muestras biológicas, dividido en dos lotes: lote 1, formado por un crío-ultramicrótomo para trabajar a temperatura ambiente y en condiciones criogénicas, junto con un procesador automático de tejidos para microscopía electrónica; y lote 2, formado por un criostato para el seccionamiento en frío de muestras biológicas. El equipamiento se instalará en el laboratorio de histología del Instituto de Investigaciones Agroambientales y de Economía del Agua (INAGEA), ubicado en la primera planta del Centre d Investigació INAGEA, en el Complex Balear de Recerca, Desenvolupament Tecnològic i Innovació (Parc Bit), Carrer Blaise Pascal, 6, Palma. El espacio dispone de suministro eléctrico estándar, disponibilidad de gases criogénicos y campana de extracción para el procesado de tejidos, por lo que no se prevén obras de adaptación. La adquisición responde a la necesidad de ampliar las capacidades del INAGEA en histología y preparación de muestras para microscopía electrónica. El crío-ultramicrótomo permitirá obtener cortes finos y ultrafinos reproducibles, principalmente de muestras biológicas incluidas en resina epoxi, tanto a temperatura ambiente como en condiciones criogénicas. El procesador automático permitirá estandarizar el tratamiento de los tejidos para su inclusión en resina y reducir la manipulación manual. Ambos equipos completarán la cadena de preparación previa al microscopio electrónico de transmisión disponible en los Servicios Científico-Técnicos de la UIB. El criostato complementará esta capacidad mediante la obtención de secciones micrométricas de muestras biológicas congeladas, necesarias para protocolos histológicos en los que se requiere preservar material fresco o evitar el procesado convencional. En conjunto, los dos lotes permitirán mejorar la reproducibilidad, reducir pérdidas de muestra y ampliar los servicios comunes de histología y microscopía ofrecidos a usuarios internos y externos. La adquisición de este equipamiento se vincula a la actuación EQC2025-009231-P, con referencia de entidad EQC2025-001078-C, concedida a la Universitat de les Illes Balears (NIF Q0718001A) para el INAGEA en la convocatoria de adquisición de equipamiento científico-técnico del año 2025, correspondiente al Subprograma Estatal de Fortalecimiento Institucional del Programa Estatal para la Investigación y el Desarrollo Experimental del Plan Estatal de Investigación Científica, Técnica y de Innovación 2024-2027.
